docs.o: The Committee of the Whole held its fourth preliminary budget hearing for fiscal year 2025 to review proposals from Human Resources, the Assessor, the Building Department, Diversity Equity and Inclusion, and the Treasurer-Collector. The council discussed the transition of pandemic-funded positions to the general fund and efforts to modernize departmental software and fee collection processes.

k: MSBA Process and Eligibility Phase Overview

docs.o: The City Council ordained a new municipal budget process ordinance, approved a CPA appropriation for Thomas Brooks Park, and endorsed state PILOT legislation for tax-exempt institutions. Councilors also acted on business permits, discussed home rule petition and committee procedures, and addressed public concerns regarding peaceful demonstrations at Tufts University.
k: Special Permit: Snappy Patties (454 High Street)
Special Permit: Pinky's Famous Pizza (165 Main Street)
CPA Appropriation: Thomas Brooks Park Phase II

Personnel Ordinance Amendment: Supervisor of Water and Sewer
Public Participation: Demonstrations at Tufts University

docs.t: City Council Committee of the Whole 04-30-24
docs.b: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
docs.o: The Committee of the Whole held its third preliminary review of the Fiscal Year 2025 budget, hearing presentations from the Recreation Department, Hormel Stadium Commission, Executive Department, and Licensing Commission. Discussions focused on department narratives, staffing requests, and facility maintenance.

The board resumed consideration of a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit application for a proposed 378-unit residential development at 280 Mystic Avenue. The board voted to authorize peer review consultants and working sessions, and continued the hearing to May 30, 2024, for a scheduling and status update.
k: Peer Review and Working Sessions Authorization

docs.o: The Medford School Committee approved the scope of a major HVAC replacement project for the Andrews and McGlynn middle schools, updated facilities and pool rental rate cards, and passed a resolution restricting future purchases of fossil-fuel building equipment. The committee also referred matters concerning capital planning, curriculum assessment reviews, and the potential co-location of the Curtis-Tufts School to subcommittees.
k: Motion to Table Resolution on Fossil Fuel Building Equipment
Resolution on the End of Fossil Fuel Building Equipment Purchases

docs.o: The board elected a new chair and adjudicated several variance and special permit requests for residential and commercial properties. Significant decisions included approving a use variance for auto sales at 38 Harvard Avenue and recognizing a pre-existing three-family use at 86 Orchard Street while denying a garage conversion at 52 Garfield Avenue.

The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals met to consider several dimensional variances and special permit applications, approving proposals for 100 Dartmouth Street, 76 Greenleaf Avenue, and 640 Boston Avenue while denying a variance for 289 Fellsway West. The board also approved previous meeting minutes and granted a continuance for 77 Shepard Road.
k: Administrative Updates and Approval of Minutes

docs.o: The Medford School Committee held a special remote meeting to appoint non-voting members to the high school building committee and review revenue strategies for the fiscal year 2025 budget.
k: High School Building Committee Non-Voting Members

docs.t: City Council Public Works and Facilities Committee 04-24-24
docs.o: The committee met to receive an update from the Department of Public Works on Medford's pavement and sidewalk management plans, reviewing infrastructure conditions, funding targets, and potential staffing for an in-house paving crew. No formal legislative action was taken.
k: Pavement and Sidewalk Management Plan Update

docs.t: City Council Planning and Permitting Committee 04-24-24
docs.o: The committee reviewed progress on comprehensive zoning ordinance revisions, focusing on site plan review structures and definition updates, and received an educational presentation from Massachusetts Housing Partnership on affordable housing financing and development.
k: Affordable Housing Training by Mass Housing Partnership

docs.t: City Council Resident Services And Public Engagement Committee 04-23-24
docs.b: CC Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee

k: Modernizing Council Communications and Outreach Strategy
Establishment of City Council Listening Sessions

docs.t: City Council Committee of the Whole 04-23-24
docs.b: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
docs.o: The Committee of the Whole held a preliminary fiscal year 2025 budget hearing featuring an overview from the finance director and initial reviews of the finance, city clerk, and city council budgets. The council approved requests for past new growth data, an update on potential FY24 department shortfalls, and an internal line-item transfer within the legislative budget.

FY25 general fund budget overview and financial update
Department budget review: Finance and procurement
Council motions on budget requests and transfer

docs.o: The board continued its comprehensive permit hearing for a 289-unit residential development at 970 Fellsway, focusing on updated architectural and site designs following peer review. The hearing was continued to May 9, 2024, to address civil engineering and traffic reviews.

The council reviewed communication strategies for public outreach and received updates on several city initiatives, including the Electrify Medford program, curbside composting, and municipal infrastructure grants.

City Councilor Matt Leming outlined a proposal to incorporate a Transportation Demand Management program into Medford's zoning recodification. The initiative aims to address traffic congestion by offering developers administrative zoning variances in exchange for transit mitigation credits.

The Medford Charter Study Committee voted to permit research into city council budget authority, tabled a motion on creating a public participation subcommittee, and approved sending draft charter Articles 2 and 3 to the Collins Center. The committee also received a presentation from the School Committee subcommittee on proposed draft language for Article 4.
k: School Committee Subcommittee Report on Article 4

docs.o: The board recommended the establishment of a new local historic district on South Street and continued the review of a mixed-use development project at 290 Salem Street.
k: Proposed South Street Local Historic District

docs.o: The Medford Liquor License Commission conditionally approved a new all-alcohol restaurant license for 25 Salem Street LLC pending updated documentation. The Commission also approved a one-day alcohol license and established a Friday deadline for future meeting application submissions.
k: One-Day Special Alcohol License for Event Them
All-Alcohol License Application for 25 Salem Street LLC

docs.t: City Council Committee of the Whole 04-17-24
docs.b: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
docs.o: The committee conducted its first preliminary budget reviews for Fiscal Year 2025 under a new city ordinance, focusing on the Council on Aging, Medford Community Media, and Veterans Services. The administration noted the city is currently working to close a budget gap caused by the expiration of one-time federal ARPA and ESSER funds.

The Council enacted a leaf blower restriction ordinance and approved a resolution pressing the MBTA to remove creosote-treated railroad ties stored along residential rail lines. It also held extensive debates regarding city infrastructure backlogs, water department management, and fire department staffing and consulting costs.

Resolution Recognizing National Animal Therapy Day
Resolution on Lawsuit Settlements and Investigations Reporting

docs.o: Danielle Balocca interviews candidate Nichole Mossalam about her run for State Representative representing Medford and Malden. Mossalam shares a personal health update, discusses her legislative priorities, and outlines upcoming campaign events.

The board reviewed civil engineering, landscape design, and a traffic peer review for a proposed 289-unit residential development at 970 Fellsway. The hearing was continued to April 23 to allow for a formal response to the traffic study findings and pending civil engineering comments.

The subcommittee reviewed and revised draft charter language for Article 4 governing the School Committee, addressing prohibitions, compensation, vacancy succession, and committee powers. The subcommittee agreed to present its draft recommendations, including a structure of four district seats and two at-large members, to the full committee.

docs.t: City Council Planning and Permitting Committee 04-10-24
docs.o: The committee met with planning consultant Innes Associates and city staff to review the three-phase roadmap for a comprehensive overhaul of the city's zoning ordinance. The committee voted to request further council input on policy items and to track related planning and economic studies within the consultant's ongoing update memo.
k: Zoning ordinance updates with Innes Associates
Motion on council input and tracking studies in memo

docs.o: The Commission approved a controversial one-year pilot program for a unified 'GL Zone' in South Medford to manage resident parking near Green Line stations. The body also authorized several residential parking variances, established no-parking safety zones at two intersections, and approved new bike lanes on Grove Street.
k: Handicap Space Relocation at 42 Riverside Avenue
No Parking Safety Zone at Fulton Street and Maple Park Avenue
No Parking Safety Zone at Bradshaw and Spring Streets

The Historical Commission considered demolition delay applications and determinations of significance for several residential properties across the city. The commission also met with Medford's new building commissioner to discuss coordination on demolition reviews and reviewed ongoing historical projects.

Demolition Applications: 18 Wedgmere Road and 9 Trout Avenue

k: Substitute Teacher Supply, Demand, and Pay Report
Medford High School Building Committee Update and Appointments

docs.t: Real Estate Transfer Fee with Kit Collins and Matt Leming
docs.o: City Councilors Kit Collins and Matt Leming discussed a proposed 0.5% to 2% fee on high-value real estate transactions to fund the city's Affordable Housing Trust. The conversation detailed the legislative path via a Home Rule petition and how the revenue would support housing production and tenant preservation.
k: Definition and Purpose of the Transfer Fee
Legislative Process for Home Rule Petitions
Affordable Housing Deficit and Legal Requirements

docs.t: WMCC First Fridays Words and Music - 04-05-24
docs.o: The West Medford Community Center hosted its First Fridays Words and Music program celebrating National Poetry Month. Former Medford Poet Laureate Terry E. Carter led readings and discussions with poets laureate C.D. Collins and Vijaya Sundaram, followed by a spoken word and jazz set performed with pianist Jonathan Fagan.
k: Discussion and Poetry Readings with Collins and Sundaram
Musical and Spoken Word Performance by The Ally Project

docs.o: The Medford Charter Study Committee reviewed Articles 2 and 3 of the draft city charter, focusing on councilor eligibility, leadership terms, and meeting procedures. Council Powers, Prohibitions, and Member Conduct

docs.o: The committee reviewed FY25 budget pressures, including $7.5 million in projected spending needs across contractual obligations, underfunded accounts, expiring ESSER funds, and new expenses. Committee Discussion on Budget Gap and Priorities

The Article 6 Subcommittee reviewed draft charter language regarding Medford's financial procedures, focusing on budget timelines, capital planning schedules, and audit oversight. The committee also considered whether to conduct further research into proposed City Council budget reallocation powers.

The Medford City Council met to consider special permits, ordinance referrals, and several state legislative resolutions, alongside major debates on public participation and housing policy. Key outcomes included referring a rental registry proposal to committee, amending council rules on public comment limits, discussing school budget deficits with local teachers, and approving climate and education resolutions.

Special Permit for Raising Cane's Signage

Tree Ordinance and Shade Tree Distribution Update

docs.o: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals reviewed four applications, granting variances for a mixed-use development on Salem Street and a residential fence, while continuing applications for used car sales on Harvard Avenue and a single-family home on Windsor Road.

The subcommittee refined specific signature thresholds and timelines across each section to present to the full Charter Study Committee.

Medical experts and community advocates gathered for a Black Health Series event focused on Alzheimer's disease, dementia diagnosis, disparities in health outcomes, and caregiver support. The subcommittee met to design a district-wide survey to assess student transportation needs and preferences before the current busing contract expires. Members discussed identifying barriers to student transit, evaluating late busing options for extracurricular activities, and addressing the impact of future high school construction on parking and bus demand.

The committee discussed technology deficiencies, poll worker training, and the status of the search for a new Elections Manager.

docs.o: The Article VI Subcommittee reviewed and drafted financial procedures for the proposed city charter, focusing on budget timelines, inter-branch collaboration, and auditing requirements. The group decided to refer a proposal concerning City Council budget amendment powers back to the full committee while establishing new requirements for joint budget meetings and digital transparency.

Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent presented the 2024-2025 middle school lottery process, which was established to address racial and socioeconomic imbalances between the Andrews and McGlynn schools. docs.o: The Community Development Board reviewed proposals for a mixed-use building on Salem Street, a large research laboratory on Commercial Street, and an auto glass repair shop. The commission approved multiple one-day licenses for community and sporting events and authorized a change of stock interest for a local business. The board also discussed the necessity of strictly enforcing the 48-hour agenda deadline for all future applications to ensure compliance with state law.

Semolina Kitchen Change of Stock Interest
